solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Check on audition and two exams

parts.note: a hearing is a legal examination of a case, the first of the two
a test is the second examination of the pair

explanation.surface: A student facing an audition plus a couple of exams wants to know how it went.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Check on audition' reads like a verb phrase about a tryout; it is the definition, audition meaning the sense of hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: An audiometric examination checks how well the ears work, and audition is an old word for that sense.

clue.text: Sound of mosquito, having leaked vital fluid, brought down

parts.note: a mosquito's whine is a hum
losing blood means one has bled

explanation.surface: A swatted mosquito, oozing blood, is knocked out of the air.
explanation.definitionFit: To be humbled is to be lowered in pride or position, a synonym for brought low.

clue.text: Make a song and dance of getting tea in right place?

indicators.note: the letter for tea is put inside the vessel named next

parts.note: a cup is the proper place for tea, so the phrase gives A CUP
T is short for tea, as in 'cha' and 'char' puzzles

explanation.surface: Someone fusses over whether the tea has been poured into the proper spot.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'right place' is a whimsical description of A CUP rather than a dictionary synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: To behave badly or attention-seekingly is to make a fuss, an idiom matching 'make a song and dance'.

clue.text: Great to swap knight for rook and take the plunge

indicators.note: chess notation gives N for knight and R for rook, so one letter is exchanged for the other

parts.note: great means very big, immense

explanation.surface: A chess player decides a bold piece exchange is the way to commit.
explanation.definitionFit: To dip or submerge oneself fully is to plunge in, so the idea of plunging matches.

clue.text: Hit on lodger over the phone

indicators.note: heard on a telephone line, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a paying lodger is a guest in the house

explanation.surface: A landlady makes a pass at her tenant during a call.
explanation.definitionFit: To hit on an idea is to arrive at it by surmise, a synonym for having worked something out by conjecture.

clue.text: In the end everyone's behind rising — true, sadly, even you!

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, taken from the word for everyone
in a down clue rising means the word for behind is read upwards

parts.note: a behind is a butt, the buttocks

indicators.note: sadly signals that the letters of true are disordered

explanation.surface: Everybody's bottom ends up in the air; true enough, and you're no exception.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns BUTT into TTUB, and 'sadly' rearranges TRUE into RUTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Caesar's Latin reproach to Brutus means 'and you too', i.e. even you have betrayed me.

clue.text: Dump ash, say, in Essex town

parts.note: a tip is a rubbish dump
an ash is an example of a tree

explanation.surface: Fly-tipping ash in an Essex town.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiptree is a village-town in Essex, England, known for its jam factory.

clue.text: Stupid, but not sick, politician found with prostitute is characteristic of malaise

indicators.note: but not means the word for sick is removed from the word before

parts.note: stupid means silly
sick means ill
MP, a Member of Parliament
tom is British slang for a prostitute

explanation.surface: A tabloid tale: a foolish MP caught with a call girl shows how sick politics is.
explanation.definitionFit: A symptom is a sign or feature indicating an illness, the characteristic of a malaise.

clue.text: Queen wearing mini-dress gets summary justice

indicators.note: wearing means having a garment on, so the queen's letter goes inside the dress

parts.note: a short shift: a shift is a simple loose dress, and a mini one is short
R is short for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: The Queen in a miniskirt meets swift punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Curt, dismissive treatment originally meant the brief time given a condemned prisoner for confession, hence rough-and-ready justice.

clue.text: EU institution's subject of conversation in tube, perhaps?

parts.note: EC, the European Commission
a topic is a subject discussed

explanation.surface: What Brussels bureaucrats chat about on the Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tube' looks like the London Underground; it is the Fallopian tube, where an out-of-place pregnancy may lodge.
explanation.definitionFit: An ectopic pregnancy develops outside the womb, most often in a Fallopian tube.

clue.text: Shout 'blast off', everyone — this'll give you a glimpse of the future!

definitions.text: this'll give you a glimpse of the future!

parts.note: to shout is to cry

indicators.note: off signals the letters of blast are out of order

parts.note: everyone is all

explanation.surface: A rocket launch countdown: shout 'blast off', everyone, and see what's coming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blast off' reads as a launch; 'off' is the anagram signal turning BLAST into STALB.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortune-teller gazes into a glass globe claiming to see coming events.

clue.text: The cow has cheek — blooming thing

parts.note: a cow is a bovine, ox
lip means cheeky talk, insolence

explanation.surface: A cheeky cow; and a mild curse, 'blooming thing'.
explanation.definitionFit: The oxlip is a flowering primula, so it is a plant that blooms.

clue.text: Two princes' mistake, in past, might end up in jam?

parts.note: Ras is an Ethiopian title for a prince
P is the abbreviation for prince

indicators.note: the word for mistake goes inside the word for past

parts.note: by means past, as in 'walk by'
to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: Two royals blundered in the past and might find themselves in a jam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jam' looks like trouble; it is the fruit preserve.
explanation.definitionFit: This soft red fruit is a classic ingredient of preserves spread on toast.

clue.text: It could be turned into toad with essential elements of spell

definitions.text: It could be turned into toad with essential elements of spell

indicators.note: being turned into something new signals the letters are rearranged
the essential part of a word is its middle, all but its ends

explanation.surface: A witch's spell turns something into a toad.
explanation.walkthrough: PEL, the middle of SPELL, joins TOAD and the seven letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A frog or toad larva grows into the adult amphibian, so it literally turns into a toad.

clue.text: Hormone store gone bad

indicators.note: gone bad means spoilt, signalling the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Hormone supplies in the stockroom have spoilt.
explanation.definitionFit: Oestrogen is the principal female sex hormone, an example of the class.

clue.text: Are you soundly sleeping? Most obstinate

parts.note: the question 'are you sleeping?' recast as 'do you rest?' turns 'are' into 'do'

indicators.note: soundly here means by sound, so the pronoun is replaced by the letter that sounds like it

parts.note: the word you is pronounced like the letter U
sleeping means resting, rest

explanation.surface: A question to a bedfellow: are you fast asleep?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Are you sleeping?' is recast as 'Do you rest?', with 'soundly' turning YOU into the letter U.
explanation.definitionFit: Dour means stern and stubborn, so the superlative is the most obstinate.

clue.text: Journalist saying what'll enable cuts to be implemented

definitions.text: what'll enable cuts to be implemented

parts.note: a hack is a journalist
a saw is an old saying, proverb

explanation.surface: A reporter describes the tool that lets budget cuts go ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cuts' suggests spending cuts; here they are literal cuts in wood or metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A hacksaw is a fine-toothed tool used for cutting through metal.

clue.text: Comic character taking us in with tart, artlessly filled with this?

indicators.note: taking signals the word for a comic character holds what follows
in confirms the pieces go inside

parts.note: a card is a joker, a comic character

indicators.note: artlessly means without art, so those letters are removed

parts.note: a tart is a pastry, taken as written here

explanation.surface: A clown takes us in with a pie, whose filling is the answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'artlessly' strips ART from TART to leave T.
explanation.definitionFit: A custard tart is a pastry case filled with egg-and-milk cream.

clue.text: Not so fast garçon is serving

parts.note: a call to stop and be patient is 'wait'
French garçon means boy, and a boy is a son

explanation.surface: A diner tells the slow waiter to be patient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'garçon' looks like the waiter; it is the French for a boy.
explanation.definitionFit: To wait on someone is to serve them at table, as a waiter does.

clue.text: In customary manner, old flame displaces you and me with no hanky-panky

indicators.note: displaces means one word takes the place of another

parts.note: in the customary manner is 'as usual'
you and me together are us
an ex is a former lover

explanation.surface: As usual, a former lover comes between a couple, and no hanky-panky follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Being without sexual feeling or activity, the term means having no sexual dalliance.

clue.text: Growth involving green shoots that rose after the budget!

definitions.text: Growth involving green shoots that rose after the budget!

parts.words: Growth involving green shoots that rose after the budget!
parts.note: a plant with green shoots, read cryptically as the price of beer that went up after the Chancellor's budget

explanation.surface: Economic green shoots and rising prices after the budget.
explanation.walkthrough: The plant's name splits into two words describing beer's price, which in Britain rises with duty in the annual budget.
explanation.definitionFit: Alecost, also called costmary, is an aromatic herb once used to flavour beer.

clue.text: British law has no right over the French — it's got strings attached

indicators.note: in a down clue over means this piece sits above the next

parts.note: UK, the United Kingdom

indicators.note: has no means the abbreviation for right is dropped

parts.note: a rule is a law
le is the French for 'the'

explanation.surface: British law trumps French law, with conditions attached.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strings attached' suggests conditions; here they are literal instrument strings.
explanation.definitionFit: The ukulele is a small four-stringed guitar-like instrument.

clue.text: Siren's degenerate depravity at work

indicators.note: degenerate signals the letters of the word for a siren are corrupted into a new order

parts.note: the word siren is used as written, its possessive adding the S
vice means depravity

explanation.surface: A siren's corrupted wickedness in action.
explanation.definitionFit: Training given while employed is described as happening during one's employment, at work.

clue.text: Tip of Union Jack seen in a British area of African capital

indicators.note: seen in signals these letters sit inside the others
the tip of each word is its first letter

explanation.surface: The end of a Union Jack flag spotted in a British part of Africa's capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Abuja replaced Lagos as Nigeria's capital city in 1991.

clue.text: Unplanned statement on campaign to free up commercial sector?

definitions.meaning: an improvised remark made without preparation

definitions.text: campaign to free up commercial sector?
definitions.meaning: read whimsically as advertising liberation, a drive for freedom for ads

explanation.surface: A politician's off-the-cuff remark about deregulating business.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase into AD, an advertisement, and LIB, short for liberation as in 'women's lib'.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking without preparation is improvising, and an off-the-cuff remark fits that improvised sense.

clue.text: You can have a riot with this — rip… ripping time!

definitions.text: You can have a riot with this

parts.note: to rip is to tear
a gas is a great time, a lot of fun

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic invitation to a riotous good time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'have a riot' looks like having fun; it means dispersing an actual riot.
explanation.definitionFit: Police use this irritant chemical spray to disperse rioting crowds.

clue.text: Result of boring maintenance instruction?

definitions.meaning: boring means drilling, and drilling for petroleum yields a shaft that produces it
a command to lubricate machinery thoroughly

explanation.surface: A tedious servicing manual produces predictable results.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' looks like dull; it means drilling into the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A drilled shaft producing petroleum, and also a two-word command to lubricate thoroughly.

clue.text: Jumping in bed with a glint, one'll get laid before the evening's over!

definitions.text: one'll get laid before the evening's over!

indicators.note: jumping signals the letters leap about into a new order

explanation.surface: A saucy picture of someone with a twinkle in the eye leaping into bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get laid' sounds risqué; a table is laid for dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: This piece of furniture is set with cutlery and plates before the evening meal.
